instructions: Dice the onion, peel and dice the carrots, and slice the celery. Drain and rinse both cans of chickpeas. Chop 1/4 cup of the parsley.

Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, celery and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Cook for 6 minutes, stirring often, until the onion is soft and the carrots are starting to give.
Add the thyme, basil and oregano and stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell them.
Add the chickpeas and the broth, turn the heat up to high, and bring it to a boil. This takes about 5 minutes.
Stir in the rotini and turn the heat down to a gentle simmer. Cook for 7 minutes, until the pasta is tender but still has a little bite. Stir once or twice so it doesn't stick to the bottom.
Take the pot off the heat. Stir in the parsley, the juice of half the lemon, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Cut the other half of the lemon into wedges. Serve with the lemon wedges.
method_notes: Simple Veganista (5.0 from 18 ratings, fewer than the 20 the rule asks for, so this is a fallback) is the lead: sauté onion, carrot and celery with dried thyme, basil and oregano, then chickpeas, rotini and liquid together for about 7 minutes. Live Eat Learn and I Heart Vegetables (both fewer than 5 ratings) simmer the broth and chickpeas first and use egg noodles; for the vegan tag this uses egg-free rotini, as the lead does, and all vegetable broth. Lemon at the end is from Simple Veganista and I Heart Vegetables. Written for 8 cups of broth and 8 oz of pasta, so it stays a soup.
